Schedule 60-min technical deep-dive with Diego and Maya (week of 11/20)
Provision trial Dedicated environment for benchmarking (2 weeks)
Confirm data residency options and KMS integration model

summary: Intro discovery on Novaplane's security gates and hosting preferences. Focus on SOC2/ISO posture, SSO/SAML, RBAC model, audit log retention, and customer-managed KMS. Agreed to a follow-up technical deep-dive and a short Dedicated trial for latency/cost validation.
topics: Encryption and KMS: CMK vs Redwood-managed keys
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-11-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Tom Evans (Novaplane Head of Security), Sara Li (CTO), Diego Ramirez (Platform Eng)

Auto-summary (auto): Quick intake, fairly noisy on one end, some transcription mistakes, but captured main asks.

00:00 Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood inference, i'm the AE on this account, quick round robin?
00:07 Tom Evans: tom evans here yep head of security at novaplane, thanks for making time, sorry if there's a bit of background noise on my side
00:13 Sara Li: sara li, cto, i've got diego on the conn— 
00:16 Diego Ramirez: yo hey, diego, platform eng, we'll mostly listen for the infra bits
00:22 Maya Patel: maya, solutions engineer, i'll cover the technical side, perf, keys, all that.

02:05 Alex Chen: high level, where are you today with inference hosting? are you self-hosting or using public endpoints?
02:13 Tom Evans: currently a mix, core models are private on prem for PII parts, but a lot of experimental endpoints hit mega cloud managed services, cost is creeping up, and we need a clear path for SOC2 and auditability for the customer data flows
02:34 Alex Chen: got it, and what are the non-negotiables for you security-wise?
02:37 Tom Evans: SOC2 Type II is required, ISO 27001 desirable but not immediate, SSO via corporate IdP with SAML, RBAC for separation of duties, strong audit logs with retention we can set, and the ability to use our KMS for CMK, we can't have plain text keys outside our control, also data residency - certain workloads must remain in eu-west-1
03:12 Maya Patel: okay that aligns with typical enterprise asks. quick clarifier — when you say CMK, do you mean customer-managed keys in your cloud KMS, HSM backed?
03:22 Tom Evans: yes, HSM backed, we want envelope encryption where tokens and any logs are encrypted with our key when at rest
03:35 Sara Li: and for latency-critical endpoints we may want dedicated capacity, but we'd like a hosted path for lower throughput features — curious about routing, fallback if dedicated misses capacity
03:49 Maya Patel: yep so redwood supports three modes — hosted api, dedicated reserved gpu pools, and private vpc/on-prem. routing policies can fallback to a compatible variant, we'll auto-failover region-wise, we can also configure model variants for cost vs latency.

06:10 Diego Ramirez: question on SAML: we enforce SCIM-based provisioning and Okta as idp, need group membership mapping into roles. how granular can the RBAC be?
06:24 Maya Patel: we support SAML SSO + optional SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based with resource scoping — you can map groups from idp to roles in redwood, and we have audit events tied to tokens and API keys, though sometimes the transcription shows 'token list' as 'tonk' — ignore that.
06:45 Tom Evans: audit logs — retention windows, can we store logs for 12 months and export to our splunk? also need immutable audit trails for compliance
06:58 Maya Patel: yes, we stream audit logs to customer destinations (s3, splunk, bigquery) with signed manifests. retention is configurable per-tenant; immutable trails supported via object lock or WORM on s3. we can also push to your SIEM via forwarders.
07:25 Alex Chen: on SOC2 artifacts — we can share a redacted SOC2 Type II report, our ISO attestation details, encryption whitepaper, and a network diagram for the private control plane, will send those after the call
07:38 Tom Evans: great, do you have a list of controls mapped to customers' purple team checks? like a control-mapping spreadsheet?
07:45 Alex Chen: yes, we have a compliance matrix mapping to common frameworks (SOC2, ISO, HIPAA notes), i'll include that.

09:10 Sara Li: for KMS, can customers bring their key into your hosted offering or only for Dedicated/Private? we prefer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) even for hosted if possible
09:22 Maya Patel: current hosted product supports customer-managed keys in the sense of envelope encryption with root-of-trust in cloud KMS for specific customers — for full BYOK hardware-backed CMK we typically recommend Dedicated or Private, because you need the key material to be under your control end-to-end. but we can engage to scope a hosted BYOK path if it's a hard requirement
09:49 Diego Ramirez: ok that matters, we need HSM-backed CMKs for some pipelines so likely we'll want Dedicated or Private for those models, but maybe host sandbox for non-PII features
10:03 Maya Patel: makes sense, we also have token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards so you can split traffic and cost across hosted and dedicated routes

12:40 Tom Evans: another question, what about pen tests and vulnerability scans? we need third-party pentest reports and annual scans, and we require notification windows for incident response
12:56 Alex Chen: we run internal pen tests annually and vendor scans, and we can provide a summary of third-party engagements; incident response SLA main points: notification within 24 hours for confirmed breaches, and we have playbooks and forensics support on enterprise tiers
13:21 Tom Evans: SLA for uptime and latency for Dedicated? we might need SLOs pinned for customer contracts
13:30 Maya Patel: Dedicated comes with contractual SLAs for throughput and latency tiers; we can pin SLOs in the reserved capacity contract. Hosted offers best-effort with published performance profiles but not the same contractual throughput guarantees

15:02 Diego Ramirez: on the logs again, are system-level logs separated from application logs? we need clear separation and different access controls
15:15 Maya Patel: yes system logs and application logs are separated. system logs are retained in the control plane with restricted access; application logs (your inference request/response traces) can be routed to your storage with the retention you choose. RBAC can gate access to those exports.
15:46 Tom Evans: about data residency — if a region is required, can you guarantee single-region hosting, and what about backups? backups must remain in-region or in a specified set of regions
15:58 Alex Chen: we can pin workloads to regions and control backup replication policies; for Dedicated and Private it's straightforward to limit cross-region replication, hosted can be configured per-account to limit to a region though multi-region failover is an opt-in.

18:30 Sara Li: curious about telemetry — we need obfuscated metrics to be shared with our product team but not contain raw prompts; can you redact or mask PII in logs before exporting?
18:44 Maya Patel: we have built-in redaction filters and tokenization hooks; additionally we recommend a prefix-KV cache to reduce exposure of raw prompts, and we can enable on-prem pre-processing for PII scrub before hitting hosted endpoints
19:06 Tom Evans: that sounds promising. can you show how redaction is configured? we might want to see a sample config and the scrubber rules
19:14 Maya Patel: i'll include sample scrubber config and docs in the follow-up bundle.

22:05 Alex Chen: any blockers to running a two-week dedicated trial for a small model set? what's your internal procurement cadence?
22:20 Tom Evans: procurement is 2-3 weeks but security sign-off is the gating factor, if we get the SOC2 artifacts and a short architecture diagram we can spin up a sandbox approval quickly. cost approvals are easier for a short eval
22:38 Alex Chen: good — we'll aim to deliver docs by friday and propose a trial start the next monday, assuming ok from your security team

28:10 Diego Ramirez: technical nit — how do you handle KV cache and warm starts for latency? we run high qps so cache efficiency matters
28:21 Maya Patel: runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache management; we can tune cache TTLs and shard placement for your workload. note sometimes the transcript will convert 'KV' to 'k v' or 'k v cache', ignore that

31:00 Tom Evans: compliance question — do you provide evidence for keys rotation and access logs to satisfy audits? auditors want a chain of custody for keys
31:12 Maya Patel: yes for Dedicated we can provide rotation logs, KMS access logs, and who/when API calls were made. For hosted, we can provide redacted KMS event logs and access records but full key material audit trails are available when you control the CMK in your cloud provider

34:40 Sara Li: any known integration issues with okta/scim? our provisioning is fairly heavy with nested groups
34:51 Maya Patel: we have customers with large scim deployments, we sometimes hit mapping limits with deeply nested groups; our config guide has patterns for flattening or mapping to role-sets — we'll share that guidance.

38:05 Alex Chen: wrap up — recap: you need SOC2 Type II + ISO docs, sample architecture, KMS integration options, RBAC mapping guide, audit log retention details, and a Dedicated trial proposal. Next step deep technical sync with diego and maya. agreed?
38:26 Tom Evans: yep agreed. please include any known limitations for hosted BYOK in the notes.
38:33 Maya Patel: will do, i'll add clear recommended pathways: hosted sandbox for non-PII, Dedicated for HSM-CMK workloads, Private for full air-gap/on-prem needs

41:00 Sara Li: timeline — security review to complete by end of month? we are aiming to put this into vendor shortlist by early december
41:12 Alex Chen: we'll try to get docs to you by 11/17 which gives you two weeks for review before your shortlist deadline
41:22 Diego Ramirez: also let's add a perf benchmark plan — small throughput tests first then 95th pct latency runs
41:30 Maya Patel: noted, i'll attach a benchmark spreadsheet and runbook.

50:05 Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the bundle and invite for the technical deep-dive, talk soon
50:15 Tom Evans: thanks all
50:18 Sara Li: thanks
50:20 Diego Ramirez: great, bye

End of transcript.

Notes: occasional mis-attributions and minor transcription errors (e.g., 'Sam L' for 'SAML', 'K-M-S' spelled out). Document links referenced during call: SOC2 redacted report (link to be emailed), compliance matrix (link), Dedicated trial proposal (link).
